value.title: Phase 3: Round two — the flake class we created, and the one product smell

sections.name: summary
sections.value: Round two: fix the flake class round one created, trace the one suspected product smell, then stop.

value.title: Fix the eight 30s-ceiling cases so they are not sitting at flake margin. THIS IS OUR OWN REGRESSION: round one killed the 5s class and created a 30s one. Prefer making the WORK cheaper over raising the ceiling again — raising it a second time concedes the pattern and buys another round of the same. The consumer's suggested cheap win: the three flow-renderer mermaid-parse cases account for ~76s between them and look consolidatable to ONE representative parse proof without losing the property under test. Verify that claim before acting on it.
value.note: DONE with a stated partial. Consumer's consolidation claim VERIFIED then declined in favour of a better fix: the cost is process SPAWNS, not assertions (measured flat — 1 fence 508ms vs 20 fences 558ms), so all three parse proofs now share ONE memoised spawn and keep every assertion rather than collapsing to one representative proof (which would have dropped the golden-corpus sweep and the importance-border regression). 3 spawns -> 1; two of the three ceiling cases stop doing work. PARTIAL, said plainly: the third still carries the single spawn at ~26s vs a 30s ceiling (~1.15x, still flake margin), and the other five ceiling cases (app x4, update-banner x1) were investigated and deliberately NOT changed — they are fully faked, 0ms locally, no spawn and no real I/O, so there is no work in them to make cheaper and no mechanism was found. EXPECTED, UNVERIFIED on win32.

value.title: Trace skills.test.ts's 10 failures to a root cause and classify: product defect or test-environment. fileURLToPath(new URL('../../../../../skills', moduleUrl)) at skills-service.ts:19 — that is src/, not test/. Do NOT assume it is a product defect because it lives in src, and do NOT assume it is environmental because it only shows on Windows. Trace it and say which, with evidence. If it IS a product defect it outranks everything else in this plan, including this phase.
value.note: CLASSIFIED: test-environment, NOT a product defect — nothing here outranks the phase. skills-service.ts:19 explains 1 of the 10 (the drive-letter-less fixture at skills.test.ts:51); the other 9 are FakeFs.copyDir comparing a POSIX-normalised needle against raw seeded keys. Traced with fileURLToPath(url,{windows:true}) over four realistic win32 module URLs — the product resolver cannot throw. 9+1=10, mechanism verified for BOTH parts. 'It is in src/' was true of FakeFs too and load-bearing for neither. Consumer's independent trace found a DIFFERENT mechanism; evidence supports (a) theirs is a real door this route never reaches, and CANNOT distinguish (c) theirs live on their tree and mine on ours. Fix landed under prime's carve-out; controls demonstrated red-before/green-after. EXPECTED, UNVERIFIED on win32.

value.title: Report the three columns for round two and state plainly whether the consumer's number moves. Round one moved it 134 -> 60. If this round moves it by ~8 (the timeouts) and the skills trace turns out environmental, say so — do not let two tasks read as more progress than the measurement supports.
value.note: REPORTED, and it says the number barely moves. FIXED 10 (skills) + 2 (flow-renderer timeouts) / DECLARED 0 / RECOVERED 0 — three columns, never a mixed total. Expected 60 -> ~48, of which 10 of ~12 are the skills fix; the skills trace came back ENVIRONMENTAL, one timeout case remains at flake margin and six ceiling cases are untouched. Denominator +1, counted from the diff — local 5124 is NOT comparable to round one's 5116 (a main merge landed between them). Local: 5124/5124 three consecutive clean runs, just checks every hard gate ok. Log: assets/tasks/phase-3/execution.log.md.
